title: pr-reviewer judgments.json
description: SSOT for the model's per-run verdicts, consumed by finalize.mjs (R5, D4). validate-judgments.mjs is a hand-written interpreter that supports a FIXED keyword subset of JSON Schema: $schema, $id, $defs, $ref, type, enum, const, properties, required, additionalProperties (boolean only), items, minItems, maxItems, minLength, maxLength, minimum, maximum, pattern, title, description. Any other keyword anywhere in this document must make validate-judgments.mjs fail closed — that is deliberate, not a gap to fill in later.

v.description: Schema version. Bump on any breaking shape change so finalize.mjs can refuse a stale judgments.json instead of misreading it.

head_sha.description: The commit SHA the model reviewed. finalize.mjs cross-checks this against the workspace HEAD before trusting anything else in the file.

candidates.description: Every finder candidate, carrying both the original finder record (finders.md) and the verifier's disposition (finding-verifier.md) in one row.

threads.description: One entry per open review thread the model classified this run (thread-resolution.md, Step 2.9c).

summary.description: The report's top-level SUMMARY scalar, authored by the model.

verdict.description: finding-verifier.md's four-way verdict. unobtainable is distinct from a null verification receipt and is capped below issue:/suggestion: severity by the verifier rule, not by this schema.

claim.description: finders.md's candidate claim — what the finder asserts is wrong.

evidence.description: finders.md's raw evidence strings, pre-verification. The verifier's OWN evidence (if any) rides in body/fence, not here.

severity_hint.description: The finder's own severity guess, prior to the verifier's severity assignment below.

verify_by.description: finders.md's verify_by — what a verifier should check to confirm or refute this candidate.

final.description: 0.4*R + 0.3*A + 0.3*Ac, per finding-verifier.md. finalize.mjs recomputes and cross-checks this rather than trusting it blindly.

blocking.description: Whether this finding is (blocking) per conventional-comments.md / severity's crosswalk.

title.description: render-comment.mjs's TITLE — required on a claim (issue:/suggestion:), forbidden on a one-liner (praise:/nitpick:/question:). That prefix-conditional rule is a domain rule validate-judgments.mjs enforces in code, since additionalProperties/required alone cannot express an if/then across sibling fields in the supported keyword subset.

materiality.description: review-config.md / diagnostic-surface.md's materiality gate — false means the finder's own judgment is that this is too minor to be worth surfacing even if verified.

category.description: A free-form, filter-matchable tag (review-config.md filters:), distinct from the fixed defect_class enum above.

unverified_reason.description: Required in spirit whenever verdict is unobtainable — enforced as a domain rule in validate-judgments.mjs, not expressible as a schema-level conditional in the supported keyword subset.

url.description: AC-11/D5: the GitHub discussion permalink for this finding, when already known (e.g. a re-review reading its own prior comment back). finalize.mjs never invents this — it is a fact carried through, never computed — and a first-review candidate omits it (execute-write-plan.mjs's own review.create response is the real source on a first post, out of finalize.mjs's scope).

fix_url.description: AC-11/D5: the pre-built Agent0 `/pr-fix` deep link for this one finding, when already assembled upstream. finalize.mjs relays it verbatim into render-comment.mjs's FIX_URL — the URL-building grammar itself stays out of scope (agents/pr-reviewer's own report-rendering.md owns it).

evidence_anchors.description: AC-11/D5: render-comment.mjs's structured EVIDENCE — additional grounding locations beyond this candidate's own path/line (e.g. a consumer site a contract break also touches). Distinct from the pre-verification `evidence` string array above.

pseudo.description: AC-11/D5: render-comment.mjs's PSEUDO — the FENCE is illustrative pseudo-code, not a literal patch.

category.description: Must equal one of gate4-scan.mjs's CATEGORIES exactly — a pre-candidate's own category, echoed back with the model's disposition.

reason.description: The prose-vs-code exemption rationale, or the confirmation rationale.

gate1.description: Description vs. code — two-state, never FAIL (a soft warning gate).

gate4.description: Self-review signals — Gate 4's PASS/FAIL is computed by finalize.mjs from these raw dispositions/findings (D6), never asserted directly by the model.

reply.description: Present only for fixed/declined/acknowledged/obsolete (Resolve-with-reply classes); persisting/unaddressed leave the thread open with no reply.

lenses.description: One log field per default-on lens (optimize-approach, standards-conformance, measurability-review, holistic-review), each render-report.mjs's ^(ran|skipped) grammar, plus the optimality proposal cards.

memory.description: Copied verbatim from MCP reads (D4) — finalize.mjs decides the lifecycle; the model never decides suppression, so these sub-objects stay permissive.
